findings.title: Cached denials mask newly granted permissions
findings.body: A denial is retained for the full cache TTL, and `Check` consults this cache before checking even a fresh permission map. If a user is denied and then granted access to that resource, every check with the same key continues to return denied until the denial entry expires, rather than using the database fallback to observe the grant. This regresses prompt visibility of newly created resources or permission changes.

findings.title: Denial cache key components can collide
findings.body: The key concatenates the resource name and parent folder with `_` but does not escape or length-prefix either component. For the same namespace, user, and action, `(name="foo_bar", parent="baz")` and `(name="foo", parent="bar_baz")` produce the same key. A denial for one resource can therefore incorrectly deny a different, permitted resource for the cache TTL.
